title: Gabriel Archangel Investments — How it works

segments.text: What if you invested only in market leaders, ranked them with one objective score, and knew your maximum loss before buying a single share?
That's exactly what Gabriel Archangel Investments does.
Here's how it works, in five simple steps.
Our starting point is simple.
Market leaders often trade close to their all-time high: the highest price the stock has ever reached.
So instead of chasing stocks that keep falling, we focus on quality companies the market is already rewarding.
Step one: the universe.
We begin with a curated list of thirty quality leaders from around the world, across technology, healthcare, industry, consumer and financial data.
Step two: fresh data, every night.
An automated process collects prices, profitability, growth and balance-sheet figures for every company, and stores the results in a scores database.
Prices refresh every fifteen minutes, fundamentals every day, and sales history every week.
Step three: the Cannon Score.
Every company receives one clear number, from zero to one hundred, built from seven factors.
Proximity to the all-time high is worth up to twenty-five points.
Return on invested capital, or how efficiently the business turns money into profit: twenty.
Sales growth over three years: twenty.
Technical strength, the stock's performance over the last twelve months: fifteen.
Net margin: ten.
Balance-sheet strength: five.
And trading volume and liquidity: five more.
Let's look at an example.
A company trading three percent below its high, earning thirty-five percent on its capital, growing sales twenty-two percent a year, and carrying little debt, scores eighty-two out of one hundred.
Any company scoring sixty or more is highlighted as a top candidate on the dashboard.
Step four: screen and compare.
Filters for distance to the high, return on capital, valuation, margins, debt and trend narrow the list down to a handful of candidates worth studying.
Step five, and the most important: how much to buy.
First, we decide the most we are willing to lose. For example, one percent of a fifty-thousand-dollar account: five hundred dollars.
If we buy at one hundred dollars and place a protective stop at ninety, we risk ten dollars per share.
Five hundred divided by ten gives us fifty shares.
If the price reaches the stop, we exit, and the loss is the five hundred dollars we planned. Profit targets are set at one, two and three times that risk.
The system also adds up the risk of every open position, so total portfolio risk is always visible.
So, in five steps:
a quality universe, fresh data every night, an objective score, focused screening, and disciplined risk on every trade.
That is how Gabriel Archangel Investments works.
Follow the leaders. Respect the risk.
